notes: Summary: Large asset manager exploring Redwood Private (VPC) for document summarization and compliance tooling. Primary concern: audit logging and SIEM integration. They require explicit log schema, guaranteed retention windows (forensically defensible), and BYOK/HSM options for model keys. SecOps prefers Splunk/QRadar ingestion via secure syslog or S3 export; compliance team flagged 5+ years retention for trade-backed logs. POC will validate: (1) event granularity (request/response metadata, user id, model version, route), (2) secure delivery to their SIEM, (3) KMS key rotation and audit trail. Notes are choppy on purpose; Peregrine repeatedly asks for sample events and end-to-end demo of log pipeline.
audit_logging_requirements: SIEM export: primary targets Splunk and IBM QRadar; acceptable transports: TLS-secure syslog (TCP 6514), S3 drop (signed PUTs + inventory), or Kafka (TLS, SASL) to their Kafka cluster

Event format: JSON with top-level fields: event_time (ISO8601), event_type, request_id, account_id, user_id (hashed), model_id, model_version, input_size_tokens, output_size_tokens, latency_ms, route, decision (fallback/cached), error_code (if any)
CEF/LEEF: SecOps can accept CEF wrapper for Splunk—provide mapping doc; prefer native JSON for richer fields

Access logs: every API operation (create, read, update, delete) for model artifacts, plus admin activity (key rotation, policy changes) must be logged; logs must include source IP, VPC endpoint id, and AWS principal ARN (or GCP identity)

Retention: baseline 1 year hot storage for search/alerts; 5 years cold storage for compliance; 7 years for trade-related transcripts (finance regulation) — support immutable retention/legal-hold toggles
Integrity: logs must be write-once (WORM) or HMAC-signed on write; provide SHA256 checksums and delivery receipts for each batch
Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery acceptable but require deduplication keys; prefer ordered append with sequence numbers for forensic reconstruction
Redaction & PII handling: offer configurable PII redaction hooks (PII pattern rules + prompt-level opt-out) and an option to store only metadata for regulated datasets

KMS integration: BYOK with HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) for envelope encryption of log payload at rest; rotation policy: customer-controlled rotation + centralized audit trail of key ops
Access controls: RBAC for log viewing; restrict raw transcript access to authenticated roles; integrate with their SSO (SAML) and enforce MFA for log access
Log schema validation: deliver a JSON schema and example event set (50 sample events) before POC; include mapping to Peregrine's Splunk fieldnames and QRadar QID mapping
Alerting hooks: provide event stream for high-severity alerts (auth failures, key use from new IP, anomaly in latency) to their SIEM via webhook or syslog
Throughput / batching: document expected log volume (estimated 20k events/day initially) and provide guidance on batching windows to meet latency/ingest cost targets
Onboarding checklist: firewall egress rules, VPC peering/VPN for syslog endpoint, service account provisioning, sample events validation, retention SLA in contract
